flagship.headline: Electric Ladyland hits No. 1 on the album chart
flagship.summary_line_1: The Jimi Hendrix Experience's Electric Ladyland reached No. 1 on the Billboard album chart dated November 16, 1968, per the Wikipedia list of Billboard 200 number-one albums of 1968.
flagship.summary_line_2: It held the top spot for two weeks and was the group's only No. 1 album, per the Wikipedia album page, and the clip below is All Along the Watchtower.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play two shows at Chicago
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones played two shows at the International Amphitheatre in Chicago on November 16, 1969, the night after Champaign, per the Rolling Stones Data chronology.
events.summary_line_2: Ike & Tina Turner and Terry Reid were among the tour's opening acts, per the Wikipedia tour page, and the clip below is Gimme Shelter, from the then-forthcoming Let It Bleed.

events.headline: Electric Ladyland hits No. 1 on the album chart
events.summary_line_1: The Jimi Hendrix Experience's Electric Ladyland reached No. 1 on the Billboard album chart dated November 16, 1968, per the Wikipedia list of Billboard 200 number-one albums of 1968.
events.summary_line_2: It held the top spot for two weeks and was the group's only No. 1 album, per the Wikipedia album page, and the clip below is All Along the Watchtower.

events.headline: Hey Jude spends its eighth week at No. 1
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' Hey Jude held No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated November 16, 1968, its eighth week on top of a nine-week run that began September 28, per the Wikipedia list of Hot 100 number ones of 1968.
events.summary_line_2: The nine weeks tied the record for the longest unbroken Hot 100 stay at No. 1, set by Percy Faith's Theme from A Summer Place in 1960, and the clip below is the song.
external_link: Wikipedia list of Hot 100 number ones of 1968

events.headline: Stevie Wonder releases Down to Earth
events.summary_line_1: Stevie Wonder's sixth studio album, Down to Earth, was released on the Tamla label on November 16, 1966, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: The first single, A Place in the Sun, came out on October 24, 1966, and the clip below is that song, one of the key Motown soul releases of the year.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play Nashville
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones played the Municipal Auditorium in Nashville on November 16, 1965, the night after Charlotte, per the Wikipedia tour page.
events.summary_line_2: The Nashville Scene described a noisy 40-minute set that ended with Get Off of My Cloud, which had just hit No. 1, and the clip below is that song.

events.headline: The Animals record Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood
events.summary_line_1: The Animals recorded Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood on November 16, 1964, with Mickie Most producing, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It was released in the UK on January 29, 1965, and reached No. 3 in the UK and No. 15 on the US Hot 100, and the clip below is the song.

events.headline: Nino Tempo and April Stevens hit No. 1 with Deep Purple
events.summary_line_1: Nino Tempo and April Stevens' Deep Purple was No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated November 16, 1963, per Billboard.
events.summary_line_2: The brother-and-sister duo revived a 1933 Peter DeRose composition and won the Grammy for Best Rock and Roll Record, per Wikipedia, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: The Beatles play Bournemouth Winter Gardens
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Winter Gardens in Bournemouth on Saturday, November 16, 1963, the 13th stop of their autumn tour, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their only appearance at that venue, and Wikipedia notes CBS filmed the show, and the clip below is Twist and Shout, a fixture of the tour set.

events.headline: The Beatles tape their second Friday Spectacular
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles recorded their second appearance on Radio Luxembourg's The Friday Spectacular at EMI House in London on November 16, 1962, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The show aired on November 23 and played both sides of their debut single, Love Me Do and P.S. I Love You, and the clip below is Love Me Do.

events.headline: Patsy Cline records I Fall to Pieces
events.summary_line_1: Patsy Cline recorded I Fall to Pieces at Bradley Studios in Nashville on November 16, 1960, with Owen Bradley producing and the Jordanaires on backing vocals, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: Released on January 30, 1961, it reached No. 1 on the Hot Country chart and No. 12 on the Hot 100, a landmark of the Nashville Sound, and the clip below is the song.
